label: lem-changing-a-function-at-finitely-many-points
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

FINDING 1
  location: step 5.1 (and the subsequent use in 5.2)
  severity: nonfatal
  claim: “Given a real η > 0, [L6] supplies N with 4K(b‑a)/ι(N) < η”
  evidence: When K = |w(p)| = 0 the inequality becomes 0 < η, which is true for any N, but the proof attempts to obtain N from L6 (cor‑archimedean‑reciprocal) by solving 4K(b‑a)/ι(N) < η, which would require division by K. L6 cannot be applied directly because it demands a positive ε. The gap is closed by a trivial case split: if K = 0 then w ≡ 0, integrable with integral 0; the rest of the proof already handles that case implicitly because all estimates become 0. A competent reader fills this in instantly.

BOUNDARY: Empty E (r = 0) is correctly subsumed under the induction base Q(0). The one‑point argument correctly accounts for points lying on partition boundaries (at most two consecutive intervals) and for endpoints a,b, which belong to exactly one subinterval. No counterexample to the public claim was found.

SOURCES: Every cited item whose full text was supplied in the dispatch (20 items) was inspected; the exact statements of the critical dependencies (thm‑riemann‑criterion, def‑darboux‑sums, def‑darboux‑integral, def‑partition‑and‑refinement, cor‑archimedean‑reciprocal, thm‑linearity‑of‑the‑integral, lem‑finite‑sum‑laws, thm‑induction‑principle, def‑countable, def‑equinumerous) match the uses in the proof steps.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered step (1.1–8.1), and Remarks.
